title: observability: token-level + KV cache metrics, dashboards and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Operators and SREs need token-level cost/latency breakdowns that include KV cache behavior so we can tune batching, cache TTLs, and alert thresholds more precisely. This PR introduces token-level metrics for KV cache hits/misses, per-route token latency buckets, tracing spans for KV lookup and cache fill, Grafana dashboard JSON for token + KV views, and an initial set of tuned alert rules.

What I changed (high level):
- Export new Prometheus metrics: rw_token_latency_seconds_bucket, rw_token_cost_tokens, rw_kv_cache_hits_total, rw_kv_cache_misses_total, rw_kv_cache_fill_duration_seconds (labels: model, route, deployment, region, cache_shard)
- Add tracing spans around KV lookup and cache fill; improved span names to make flamegraphs meaningful
- New Grafana dashboard JSON: token-level cost/latency + KV cache hit-rate, heatmaps per model/route, and top-N slow routes panel
- Alert rules in alerts/token_level_alerts.yaml: adjusted thresholds for P95/P99 token latency; KV miss-rate alert with severity scaling and auto-snooze notes for cold-starts
- Docs: docs/observability/alert_tuning.md describing how thresholds were chosen and how to iterate using sample workloads
- Tests: unit tests for metrics registration and a small integration smoke test that validates metrics emitted for a synthetic workload

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics registered and exported (unit tests)
- [x] Tracing spans added and validated locally with jaeger dev stack
- [x] Grafana dashboard JSON added and renders in staging Grafana
- [x] Alert rules validated using replayed metrics in staging
- [x] Docs updated with tuning guidance

Backward compatibility: All new metrics are additive and use stable names; no removals or breaking label changes.

Rollout plan: feature flags gate the enhanced metrics and tracing for low-traffic customers initially (controlled via config flag observability.token_kv_enabled). Gradual rollout to 25% of production traffic for 48 hours, then 100% if no regression. Alerts are staged in Prometheus as WARN-level first, then promoted to PAGER after 72h of stable thresholds.

Notes: The initial KV miss-rate threshold is conservative (5% for sustained 10m window) to avoid noise from cold-starts. See docs/observability/alert_tuning.md for methodology and sample queries.
